what: The ID builder dropped the word 'to', so addContactToList became add_contact_list, which reads as 'add a contact list'.
fix: Keep 'to' and 'for' in IDs. Read a sample of generated entries after every generator change.

what: The hint that tells an agent how to find a list ID pointed to 'Get lists in a folder', which itself needs a folder ID, instead of 'Get all the lists'. The lookup took the first match.
fix: Prefer the route with the fewest path parameters, then the shortest path.

what: A code formatter split a one-line set over many lines, so a text replacement in the generator silently changed nothing. The regenerated IDs were the same as before.
fix: Edit only after reading the formatted file, and check the generated output after every change.

what: The plan assumed an API key on day one. Creating an API key requires a verified phone number.
fix: Recorded as a precondition of creating an API key and of sending a campaign (catalog/curation.yaml). The human started phone verification.

what: Phone verification by SMS and by call did not work for this account. A request is open with Brevo support.
fix: Verification moved to the routes the web app uses. Actions with only a documented route stay 'documented' until a key exists.

what: To test the web app's internal routes from a script, the agent reused the browser's session cookies outside the browser. The web session ended right after. The cause is not confirmed: the session may be bound to the browser that created it.
fix: Never reuse session cookies outside the browser. The exported cookie file was deleted and the human logged in again.

what: The agent assumed a fetch from the page's own JavaScript would carry the login. The internal services answered 403 'Cookie auth cookie missing'.
fix: UI-only actions are verified through the UI itself, with the app's own network calls captured as evidence.

what: The secret scanner flagged its own file, because the file holds the patterns it searches for.
fix: The scanner skips its own file. A drift test showed the ledger check fails when the table is stale and passes after a render.

what: Check L001 failed on 7 entries, for example: ID drops ['by'] from operationId getExternalFeedByUUID; ID drops ['all'] from operationId getAllExternalFeeds; ID drops ['by'] from operationId getInboundEmailEventsByUuid.
fix: The ID builder now drops only a, an, the and plural s. 'getScheduledEmailById' becomes get_scheduled_email_by_id. Closed by L001 on the next build.

what: Check L002 failed on 14 entries, for example: finder brevo.contacts.get_contact_stats itself needs ['identifier']; finder brevo.conversations.get_automated_message itself needs ['id']; finder brevo.conversations.get_message itself needs ['id'].
fix: A finder must list the entity without any other ID. When the API has no such route, find_with is empty, so the agent takes the ID from the create response instead of a circular lookup. Closed by L002 on the next build.

what: Check V-contacts-lifecycle failed on 1 entries, for example: step list_has_contact (brevo.contacts.get_contacts_from_list): no item with email='zz-catalog-test-1793635604@example.com' in contacts.
fix: Check V-contacts-lifecycle passes again at commit 9b16cb4.

what: Check V-crm-lifecycle failed on 1 entries, for example: step read_task_done (brevo.tasks.get_task): done = False, expected True.
fix: Not a code error: Brevo accepts done=true, sets a completion time (DoneAt), and leaves done false. The CRM scenario records it on every run: rename_task and read_task_renamed are the positive control (the same call does change the name), and read_task_done_at checks DoneAt. The catalog marks brevo.tasks.update_task as failed with this evidence.

what: The CRM scenario named two action IDs that do not exist in the catalog: the task-types read and the deal-link action. The executor stopped with 'unknown action'.
fix: Every scenario action ID was checked against catalog/index.json. tools/presubmit_check.py now fails on an unknown ID. A negative control with a wrong ID failed as expected.

what: The builder showed brevo.tasks.update_task as verified, because the write returned 204. Its read-back failed, but the failure was filed under the read action (get_task), which had passed in other steps.
fix: Read-back steps now name the write they check (postcondition_of). A failed read-back marks that write failed. tests/test_postcondition_attribution.py replays the case.

what: The builder marked two list actions failed (get_webhooks, get_transac_emails_list) because a call with no inputs returned 400. Both work with data present or with a filter. The 400 is what an agent gets with no setup, not a broken action.
fix: Both now run in a scenario with setup and are verified. The builder keeps the bare-call error in the entry notes, so an agent knows to pass a filter or to expect 400 on an empty account.

what: Two actions that delete data had no confirmation flag: delete_hardbounces (an empty call clears every hard bounce) and batch_delete_object_records. The generator asked for confirmation only on the delete class, and both are class 'action'.
fix: The generator now asks for confirmation on any action whose name deletes, removes, cancels, revokes or clears. New lint check L007 catches the class, with a test. 73 actions now ask first (was 67).

what: get_inbound_email_events_by_uuid told the agent to find the uuid with brevo.event.get_events, a different product (custom contact events). The path /inbound/events was named 'event'.
fix: The entity is now inbound_email_event, so the finder is brevo.inbound_parsing.get_inbound_email_events. The same mix-up had given create_event a wrong read-back (the inbound uuid read), so create_event and create_batch_events now show as lint gaps G001 instead of a wrong check. add_contact_to_list and remove_contact_from_list are now each other's undo.

what: get_webhooks hid two facts an agent needs: the type input defaults to transactional, so other webhook types stay hidden, and its note did not say that the 400 meant no webhooks existed.
fix: The note now says to call once per type and that the 400 means none. The builder states when the bare call ran (before any test data existed).

what: create_segment had no input for the segment rules, and its read-back passes for a segment with no rules. An agent could save a segment of all contacts and report success.
fix: The entry now says the rule format is unknown (the request body was not captured), that a browser agent must set the rules, and that the read-back proves the name only. Capturing the body is in the next steps.

what: The catalog was built from the API spec first, and the web app walk listed only 24 buttons. The brief asks for everything a user can do by clicking around the product. A full walk of the web app found 107 business actions, and only 59 of them (55%) matched a catalog action.
fix: Walked every menu page, row menu and bulk action with one test item of each kind. sources/ui/ui_map.yaml joins each UI action to the catalog: matches get a ui_path route, the 46 others are new 'seen' or 'gated' actions. coverage.json now reports the web app coverage, and a test covers the join.

what: PLAN.md said the deadline was confirmed with the recruiter ('I asked to confirm'). The email thread shows no such question.
fix: PLAN.md now gives the date from the recruiter's email and makes no claim about a confirmation. The README lists every assumption in one place.

what: 11 of the 31 verified writes had no read-back linked to them. The builder set verified from the write's own 2xx. The README said every write was read back.
fix: Each scenario read step now names the write it checks, and remove_contact_from_list and delete_attribute got new read-back steps (with a list_excludes check). The builder no longer sets verified on a write without a passing read-back, with a test. All 4 scenarios ran again: 31 of 31 verified writes have a passing read-back.

what: The README counted 10 web app actions as runnable through internal calls (it was 7) and 61 of 107 as covered before the walk (it was 59). The email said two list calls need a filter (it was one) and that the walk covered every page.
fix: The builder now counts each UI action by the route its catalog action really has, and separates actions the walk added. README and email numbers now come from catalog/coverage.json.

what: Commit 95103cc said it stopped tracking two plugin session files, but they were still tracked. A git stash and stash pop for the clean-clone test had undone the git rm --cached.
fix: The files are now removed from the index, and the commit was checked with git ls-files.

what: Check L006 failed on 1 entries, for example: generator source changed but its output is identical.
fix: False alarm: this edit removed an unused index file, a refactor that changes the generator but not its output on purpose. L006 cannot tell that apart from an edit that had no effect, so a pure refactor opens an entry that must be closed by hand with this reason.

what: The README and email said every MCP run returns a read-back, but 4 verified writes (add_contact_to_list among them) had no read-back in their entries. Lint check G001 skipped the action class, so it did not count them.
fix: The builder now copies each passing scenario read-back into the entry it checks: 31 of 31 verified writes carry one. G001 now covers every write. The README says when a run has no read-back.

what: Several claims went beyond the evidence: update_task 'did nothing' (it sets a completion time), the phone check 'is a precondition in the catalog' (no entry had it), e-commerce 'blocked by the plan' (it needs activation), a read-back delay of 'a few seconds' (never measured), and update_company and create_note with spec success codes that the live API does not return.
fix: Each claim now matches its evidence. The builder records the live success code and a note when it differs from the spec. catalog/curation.yaml adds the phone precondition with its source.

what: Code defects: the walk kept only the first UI path per action; a failed read-back could mark the read action failed; list_excludes passed on a missing path; tools/catalog_lint.py had no entry point, so running it checked nothing; run_action exited when the build folder was absent; the confirmation rule missed dissociate, disable and unlink.
fix: Each one is fixed, and tests cover the UI paths, the read attribution, the newest result winning, missing paths, gated refusals and search ranking (23 tests). The lint command now prints its findings and exits 1 on an error.

what: The read-backs copied in the previous round gave an agent nothing to check ('add_contact_to_list took effect', 'the read-back step attribute_listed passes'). A missing API key made the MCP server exit. Five fixes had no test that failed when they were reverted. An older read probe could hide a newer failure, and the walk counts were taken before the evidence.
fix: Read-backs are now written from the scenario's own check (for example '`contacts` holds an item whose `email` is the one that was sent'). A missing key is a refusal with the reason. The newest own result wins over probes, and the walk counts come after the evidence. Tests cover most of these fixes. The order of steps in build_catalog.main() has no test.

what: Claims still went past the evidence: 7 actions 'run through the web app internal calls' (only a browser agent can run them), the walk 'opened every page' of the settings menu (several sections were only listed), a stale 57%, '46 web app actions are seen or gated' (48 are), and the email said every reviewer finding was fixed (the minor ones are listed as gaps).
fix: README and email now say what the evidence shows, and the settings sections the walk did not open are listed in the gaps.

what: Search ranked delete_folder (which deletes a folder and all its lists) first for 'Delete the contact list named ...', and create_list first for the demo's add request, while the README said the right action came first. The missing-key test stubbed the function it was meant to test, and the update_task note cited a run that did not record the completion time.
fix: Search now weighs the request's own entity and leading verb; 15 requests, including the 4 demo requests word for word, rank the right action first in tests. The key test runs the real lookup with no key. The CRM scenario now records the completion time and a rename control, and the note cites that run.

what: More claims past the evidence: the settings sections the walk did not open were only partly listed; the email said the walk covered 'the 40 pages of the main and settings menus'; 'Invite a user' was counted as seen in the web app although the walk never opened the Users page; the AI log said the walk 'visited every menu area'.
fix: README lists all 19 settings sections that were not opened, the email says the walk opened 40 pages, the invite row is out of the count (106 web app actions now), and the AI log wording matches the walk.

what: 40 writes that nothing in the catalog undoes ran without confirmation, for example import_contacts, edit_user_permission and create_sender, although the README said confirmation covers account settings. The executor also sent any inputs: an unknown key went into the request body, and a missing required input reached Brevo.
fix: The generator asks for confirmation on every write it cannot undo (155 actions now). The MCP server and the CLI check the inputs against the entry's schema before any call. The rule seen live for the transactional log (one of email, messageId or templateId) is now in that schema (catalog/curation.yaml).

what: The schema resolver counted every level of JSON, so below depth 6 it replaced keyword values: listIds items lost "type": "integer". 69 input schemas were not valid JSON Schema. Found while adding input checks.
fix: The resolver counts only reference hops (at most 6). All 348 input schemas are now complete and valid.

what: Claims past the evidence: '106 business actions' counted buttons, which map to 93 catalog actions. 'Most corrections led to a check' when the ledger named a check for 8 of 32. The README said the MCP server enforces rules an agent cannot skip, but confirmed=true is the agent's own flag and a failed action still runs. The PDF renumbered a list with sub-items.
fix: The README and the email give both counts (106 buttons, 93 catalog actions), the ledger names the check for each correction that has one, the README says the server applies the rules and states the limits, and the list renders as one item.

what: The new input check read oneOf as anyOf, so any body passed for add_contact_to_list and remove_contact_from_list, for example {} or {"emails": []}. A timeout after the request was sent was reported as 'did not run', although a create may have landed. Lint checks L007 to L009 never opened a ledger entry and presubmit did not run the lint. A '+' in a path went to Brevo raw, which no live call had proven. The new tests could reach the live account if a fix regressed.
fix: Each one-field oneOf branch now requires its field, and the server names the fields it needs. A connection error is a refusal; a write with no answer is 'unknown' and names the check to run before a retry. The build syncs every lint error check and presubmit runs the lint. Paths encode '+'. The MCP tests run with a client that fails on any request.

what: Follow-ups on the previous fix: after a create with no answer, the server named a read-back that needs the ID the lost response held (create_list pointed to get_list, which needs listId). A response that could not be decoded escaped as an exception. A named but malformed field ({"emails": "x"}) got the branch list instead of the real cause.
fix: When the read-back needs an input the write did not send, the reply names the finder for it. Every request error is caught, and a write gets 'unknown'. The input check reports the malformed value of the named field.
